title: SFX Kit sounds
description: The SFX Kit catalogue: the kit's rules for using its sounds, its categories, and a record for every sound with what it is, when to use it, how to place it in time and how loud it is.

credit.description: Credit isn't required; this is how to give it if you'd like to.

how_to_use.description: How to read and use the data, in brief: find, place, fit, levels and tuning. GUIDE.md has it in full.

loudness.description: How the kit's levels are measured and set.

id.description: The category's id, as each sound's category field gives it.

dimensions.description: What sets the category's sounds apart (speed, intensity, kind…) and each one's values, in order.

labels.description: Display names for some dimension values.

id.description: Stable identifier; also the file's name.

file.description: Path to the WAV, from the kit's root.

variant.description: Its place in its category's dimensions (for example speed: fast, intensity: soft).

channels.description: 1 for mono; 2 for stereo (centred, with width, never panned).

sync.description: Where the sound meets the picture. Start the sound at (the moment it should meet) minus sync.at: the one rule for every sound.

at.description: The sync point: seconds from the file's start to the part of the sound that should meet the moment. That's its loudest moment for most sounds, its very start for a gesture that runs with an action, its first event for a sequence, or the part that matters for a sound in parts (see parts).

meets.description: The kind of moment the sync point meets: instant (the frame something happens), action-start (the frame an action begins; the sound runs with it), move-peak (a move's fastest point), arrival (what a build leads to: the reveal, the cut, the landing) or release (the frame something is let go, dropped or sent off).

how.description: That moment, in words, for this sound.

parts.description: For a sound in distinct parts: each part and when it comes, in order.

timing.description: More of the sound's shape, in seconds from its start.

audible_start.description: Where it first comes within 40 dB of its peak.

onset.description: Where it first comes within 20 dB of its peak.

peak.description: Its loudest moment. Place by sync.at, not this: they differ for every sound that doesn't anchor on its loudest moment.

body_end.description: Where it last falls 20 dB under its peak.

audible_end.description: Where it last falls 40 dB under its peak.

span_seconds.description: For a sound that runs with an action, builds up to an arrival or follows a release: the length of moment it fits at rate 1. To fit a moment exactly, set the rate to span_seconds divided by the moment's length.

fits_seconds.description: The shortest and longest moment it fits, within its rate range: the action a gesture runs with, the lead-up to a build's arrival, the fall or exit after a release, or the move a whoosh rides. Hits, pops and clicks don't have one.

lufs.description: Loudness over its loudest 150 ms, K-weighted, in LUFS.

tier.description: Its loudness tier in its category.

under_voiceover_db.description: How far it comes down (dB) wherever its body (timing.onset to timing.body_end) overlaps speech, for the voice to stay clear over it.

rate.description: How far it can be slowed or sped up (playback rate; its pitch and its times move with it: divide the times by the rate). [1, 1] means don't change it: it's tuned, or its pitch must stay true.

notes.description: How to fit it to other lengths.

tuning.description: For a tuned sound, the notes it uses: C major pentatonic (only C, D, E, G and A, which also sit with music in G or F major, or A, E or D minor), C major (a B or an F as well), or one note (C, for the 808-style basses).

pairs_with.description: Categories it layers well with, and how.

character.description: A word or two on its tone.
